whole_original_publication_typed_object.title: A singleton-supported cycle correction to Byrnes's differential-poset bound
whole_original_publication_typed_object.author: Alec Kriebel
whole_original_publication_typed_object.description: An explicit singleton-supported cycle correction improves Byrnes’s cumulative differential-poset bound, with a sharp coefficient and conditional equality results.
whole_original_publication_typed_object.abstract: For every ordinary unweighted r-differential poset and n ≥ 2, we subtract an explicit nonnegative term from Byrnes's cumulative upper bound for the nth rank size. The term is the cycle rank of the preceding incidence subgraph supported on elements with a singleton successor. Singleton witnesses transfer these cycles into the next incidence graph by replacing stars with trees having the same terminals. The correction can be positive and attained on standard reflected Young-prefix examples, and its coefficient one is sharp. A singleton-successor condition gives the conjectured local recurrence; two such successors give a conditional equality characterization. The result answers the printed request for an improvement of Byrnes's inequality in an incidence-dependent form. It does not prove the general local recurrence, improve the global Fibonacci envelope, or give a combinatorial proof of strict rank growth.

metadata.title: A singleton-supported cycle correction to Byrnes's differential-poset bound
metadata.description:
For every ordinary unweighted r-differential poset and n at least 2, an explicit nonnegative singleton-supported cycle rank q_n is subtracted from Byrnes's cumulative upper bound. The correction depends only on the two preceding incidence ranks. Terminal-preserving witness trees prove the cycle transfer b_n at least q_n. Standard reflected Young-prefix examples attain strict improvements from 31 to 30 for r=3 and from 20 to 19 for r=1, making coefficient one sharp. A singleton-successor sufficient condition, conditional two-witness equality characterization and the all-r rank-three consequence are proved.

This answers Majumder's printed request for an improvement of the Byrnes inequality in an incidence-dependent form. Stanley's general local recurrence, the separate combinatorial strict-growth-proof question and improvement of the global Fibonacci envelope are not claimed. Classical incidence identities, graph facts, singleton methods and Wagner reflection are credited. Gaetz-Venkataramana Proposition 3.4 already gives the exact rank-one two-singleton lemma used in the rank-three deduction; the witness poset families are standard. A dated bounded primary-source comparison found no earlier equivalent supported-cycle upper-bound theorem in inspected material; historical firstness, a new general method and present worldwide openness are not certified.

The deposit consists of a seven-page paper and a complete editable-source/verification ZIP, preserving all eight original submitted artifacts. Portable standard-library exact checks, complete expected outputs, closed manifests and a local rebuild script are included. Finite computations supplement the written universal proof and do not certify full recurrence or literature absence. AI tools were extensively involved in research planning, mathematical exploration and proof development/reconstruction, computation, source and literature investigation, writing, editing and adversarial verification. Alec Kriebel is the named human author. This work is unrefereed, without professional independent human peer review, journal acceptance or formal proof-assistant certification; internal AI reviews do not supply those certifications.

claim.category: Ordinary unweighted r-differential posets with one minimum, finite ranks and integer DU-UD=rI at every rank including0.
claim.quantifiers: Every positive integer r, every such poset, every n>=2.
claim.support: S consists of z in P[n-2] having an upper a in P[n-1] whose entire predecessor set is {z}; H_S retains all P[n-1], including isolates.
claim.universal_theorem: 0 <= q_n=beta(H_S) <= b[n-1] and b[n] >= q_n; p[n] <= U_n-q_n = r*p[n-1]+p[n-2]+b[n-1]-q_n.
claim.conditional_consequences: If all centers are supported the local recurrence holds for every admissible next extension. For n>=3 under the stated two-singleton hypothesis equality iff reflection up to upper-rank relabelling; this implies the all-r rank-three bound with exact reflection equality.
claim.sharpness: Classical reflected Y^3 and reflected Young prefixes extend infinitely, attain q=1 corrections30/31 and19/20, and disprove every coefficient c>1.

broader_question_limits.general_local_recurrence: Not established or claimed. It would require b[n]>=b[n-1]; unremoved allowance is exactly b[n-1]-q_n.
broader_question_limits.strict_residual_example: Young n6: b5=1, q6=0, refined13, local12, actual11. This is not a counterexample to the local recurrence.

materially_distinct_families.mechanism: Integer commutator including rank0, unique minimum, finite ordinary ranks; descent excludes repeated common covers.

Both actual graphs contract by forests to the same labelled terminal graph.
Signed path map has zero boundary and uniquely recoverable nonwitness coefficients over every field.

Actual Gaetz–Venkataramana v3 Prop3.4 and direct disjoint-subset count provide >=2 singleton successors at rank1.

materially_distinct_families.mechanism: Direct reflection preserves ordinary axioms indefinitely; attained q1 examples defeat every real c>1.

whole_original_public_sections.heading: What this means
paragraphs: A graded poset is arranged in ranks, with edges recording which elements cover those immediately below. Its rank sizes count the elements at each level. Differential posets satisfy a precise balance between the upward and downward edges.

Byrnes’s cumulative bound limits the size of the next rank using earlier rank sizes. This note subtracts a correction that can be read from the preceding incidence graph. Certain cycles are forced to survive into the next rank, leaving less room for new elements. The correction may be zero; classical examples show that it can also give a strict, attained improvement.

whole_original_public_sections.heading: The full bound
paragraphs: Fix any positive integer r and any ordinary unweighted r-differential poset P: a locally finite poset graded by the nonnegative integers, with one minimum and finite ranks. Its ordinary up and down operators over ℚ satisfy DU−UD = rI at every rank, including rank zero, as an equality of integer incidence counts. Put pⱼ = |Pⱼ|. Zero common covers are allowed; an identity interpreted only modulo a characteristic is not the category used here.
For j ≥ 1, let Bⱼ be the bipartite cover graph on Pⱼ₋₁ ⊔ Pⱼ and let bⱼ = β(Bⱼ), where β(H) = |E(H)|−|V(H)|+c(H) and c(H) counts every component, including isolated vertices.

For n ≥ 2, let S consist of z ∈ Pₙ₋₂ having some a ∈ Pₙ₋₁ with the entire predecessor set pred(a) = {z}. Such an a is a singleton successor of z; this does not mean that z has only one successor. Let Hₛ retain S, every vertex of Pₙ₋₁, and the incident edges between them. Set qₙ = β(Hₛ).
The theorem holds for every such r, P and n: 0 ≤ qₙ ≤ bₙ₋₁ and bₙ ≥ qₙ. Thus, writing Uₙ = 1 + r Σ_{k=0}^{n−2} pₖ + (r−1)pₙ₋₁,
pₙ ≤ Uₙ−qₙ = r pₙ₋₁ + pₙ₋₂ + bₙ₋₁−qₙ.
The correction depends only on the two preceding incidence ranks, before Pₙ is constructed. No additional singleton-support hypothesis is needed for this bound.

whole_original_public_sections.heading: Why the cycles transfer
paragraphs: The full consecutive-rank incidence graphs are connected. Their edge counts give the exact slack identities pₙ = Uₙ−bₙ and bₙ−bₙ₋₁ = r pₙ₋₁+pₙ₋₂−pₙ.

Choose a singleton witness a_z for each supported z. The common-cover identity supplies upper vertices joining that witness to the other successors of z. Their complete stars form a tree with precisely those terminals. Different supported centers cannot share an internal upper vertex: that would give a common successor to witnesses whose predecessor sets are disjoint.

Consequently all these tree replacements coexist inside the next incidence graph. They preserve the terminal connections and change edge and vertex counts equally, including a one-terminal tree. Retaining all remaining terminal isolates preserves the component count too. Their union therefore has cycle rank qₙ, so the next full graph has at least that cycle rank. The argument works for arbitrary witness choices; finite checks supplement the written proof.

whole_original_public_sections.heading: When the local recurrence and equality follow
paragraphs: If every z ∈ Pₙ₋₂ has at least one singleton successor in Pₙ₋₁, then Hₛ is the whole preceding incidence graph and qₙ = bₙ₋₁. The theorem then gives pₙ ≤ r pₙ₋₁+pₙ₋₂ for every admissible next extension. In particular, the condition holds whenever rank n−1 was formed by reflection-extension; rank n need not itself be reflected.

For n ≥ 3, suppose every such z has at least two distinct singleton successors. Equality in the local bound holds if and only if the extension to rank n is reflection-extension, up to relabelling that new rank. The two-singleton and n ≥ 3 hypotheses belong to this equality statement; one witness alone is not asserted to characterize equality.

Gaetz–Venkataramana’s established rank-one two-singleton lemma supplies these hypotheses at rank three. Hence for every positive integer r, p₃ ≤ r p₂+r, with equality precisely when rank three is obtained by reflection from rank two. The lemma is credited, rather than presented as new.

whole_original_public_sections.heading: Two classical examples and the sharp coefficient
paragraphs: Wagner reflection adds one upper vertex over each previous neighborhood and r singleton successors over each current element. It preserves the ordinary differential-poset identities and can be repeated indefinitely. The following are classical reflected Young-prefix constructions, used here as witnesses rather than new poset families.
For r = 3, take the Y³ prefix with ranks (1,3,9), reflect to obtain rank size 30, and continue reflecting. Here q₃ = b₂ = b₃ = 1: Byrnes’s bound 31 is reduced to the attained bound 30.

For r = 1, take Young’s lattice through rank five, reflect twice, and continue reflecting. The ranks are (1,1,2,3,5,7,12,19), with q₇ = b₆ = b₇ = 1. Byrnes’s bound 20 is reduced to the attained bound 19. Both finite prefixes therefore belong to infinite differential posets.

In each example pₙ = Uₙ−qₙ with qₙ = 1. Replacing coefficient one by any real c > 1 would demand pₙ ≤ Uₙ−c qₙ < pₙ. Coefficient one is sharp; this does not claim optimality among all possible uses of preceding incidence data.

whole_original_public_sections.heading: The remaining gap and boundary cases
paragraphs: The unremoved allowance is exactly bₙ₋₁−qₙ. In Young’s lattice at n = 6, b₅ = 1 and q₆ = 0: the refined bound is 13, the proposed local bound is 12, and the actual rank size is 11. This is not a counterexample to the local recurrence. The general recurrence would still require bₙ ≥ bₙ₋₁.
At n = 2, q₂ = 0 and p₂ ≤ r²+1. For r = 1 the replacement may be a single terminal with no internal vertex. Empty S leaves all Pₙ₋₁ vertices isolated and gives qₙ = 0; b₁ = 0 and no b₀ is assumed.

The result does not prove the general local recurrence, improve the global Fibonacci envelope, or provide a combinatorial strict-growth proof. The usual strict-growth statement also has the bottom exception r = 1 with p₀ = p₁ = 1. Weighted or multiple-edge graphs, merely modular commutation and isolated locally commuting layers without a valid bottom rank are outside the theorem.

Historical firstness, independence from unknown work and present worldwide openness are not established. The source comparisons are bounded, with version and access limits; a later proof, uninspected publisher edition or unpublished work is not ruled out.

whole_original_public_sections.heading: Context and credit
paragraphs: Majumder’s contribution in Oberwolfach Report 23/2018, printed pages 1452–1453, separately asks for an improvement of Byrnes’s cumulative inequality toward the local bound and for a combinatorial strict-growth proof. This note addresses the improvement request in an incidence-dependent form; the request imposes no rank-number-only restriction.

Stanley’s operator framework and Wagner reflection, Byrnes’s cumulative bound and earlier cycle arguments, and Stanley–Zanello’s incidence and hypergraph sums are established background. Cycle-space inclusion and terminal-preserving tree replacement are elementary graph facts. The assertion here is their simultaneous singleton-supported transfer in the ordinary differential-poset setting.

Singleton and crown methods also have Lewis and Miller–Reiner antecedents. Gaetz–Venkataramana’s Proposition 3.4 in the inspected v3 preprint is the exact rank-one lemma used above. Qing and Wright concern related upper-extremal scopes; Miller’s strict-growth work is a different direction. Versioned preprints and the published records are distinguished in the source dossier; no unread final-body identity or exhaustive literature coverage is inferred.

whole_original_public_sections.heading: Read the paper
paragraphs: Read the complete unchanged seven-page published paper below, or open and download the original PDF. The complete source-and-verification ZIP includes the editable manuscript, authored supporting history and optional exact finite checks. The universal theorem and infinite realization rest on the written proofs.

paragraphs: Independent verification of the transfer and equality arguments, a substantive primary-source comparison, or work toward a journal submission would be welcome. Any eventual authorship would reflect actual mathematical or writing contributions agreed together.

records.full_printed_abstract: For every ordinary unweighted r-differential poset and n ≥ 2, we subtract an explicit nonnegative term from Byrnes's cumulative upper bound for the nth rank size. The term is the cycle rank of the preceding incidence subgraph supported on elements with a singleton successor. Singleton witnesses transfer these cycles into the next incidence graph by replacing stars with trees having the same terminals. The correction can be positive and attained on standard reflected Young-prefix examples, and its coefficient one is sharp. A singleton-successor condition gives the conjectured local recurrence; two such successors give a conditional equality characterization. The result answers the printed request for an improvement of Byrnes's inequality in an incidence-dependent form. It does not prove the general local recurrence, improve the global Fibonacci envelope, or give a combinatorial proof of strict rank growth.
records.full_native_deposit_description_HTML:
For every ordinary unweighted r-differential poset and n at least 2, an explicit nonnegative singleton-supported cycle rank q_n is subtracted from Byrnes's cumulative upper bound. The correction depends only on the two preceding incidence ranks. Terminal-preserving witness trees prove the cycle transfer b_n at least q_n. Standard reflected Young-prefix examples attain strict improvements from 31 to 30 for r=3 and from 20 to 19 for r=1, making coefficient one sharp. A singleton-successor sufficient condition, conditional two-witness equality characterization and the all-r rank-three consequence are proved.

This answers Majumder's printed request for an improvement of the Byrnes inequality in an incidence-dependent form. Stanley's general local recurrence, the separate combinatorial strict-growth-proof question and improvement of the global Fibonacci envelope are not claimed. Classical incidence identities, graph facts, singleton methods and Wagner reflection are credited. Gaetz-Venkataramana Proposition 3.4 already gives the exact rank-one two-singleton lemma used in the rank-three deduction; the witness poset families are standard. A dated bounded primary-source comparison found no earlier equivalent supported-cycle upper-bound theorem in inspected material; historical firstness, a new general method and present worldwide openness are not certified.

whole_original_publication_typed_object.title: An exact period criterion for focal-distance products in elliptic billiards
whole_original_publication_typed_object.author: Alec Kriebel
whole_original_publication_typed_object.description: An exact least-period criterion classifies when ordinary focal-distance products are constant in noncircular elliptic billiards, including primitive windings and repetitions.
whole_original_publication_typed_object.abstract: For a noncircular elliptic billiard with a strictly nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic, we prove that the product of ordinary distances from all vertices to either fixed focus is independent of phase if and only if the least period is 2 modulo 4. This proves the least-period interpretation of entry k₁₁₄ in Reznik–Garcia–Koiller's list of unproved invariants and classifies every other primitive period and every repeated traversal. The proof identifies the complete divisor of the focal-distance factor in the classical Jacobi parameter. An exact doubled-triangle example shows why a condition on return length alone is insufficient. The parametrization, identities and divisor method are established tools. This AI-assisted research note is unrefereed.
whole_original_publication_typed_object.abstract_source: complete printed TeX/PDF abstract, not native deposit description
whole_original_publication_typed_object.native_deposit_description_html:
For a noncircular elliptic billiard with a strictly nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic, the product of ordinary distances from all vertices to either fixed focus is independent of phase if and only if the primitive least period is congruent to 2 modulo 4. The result covers all admissible primitive star turns and both orientations. For every even least period, the two focal products are equal at each phase. Repetitions raise the positive primitive product to an integer power, so listed return length alone is insufficient. Circles are treated separately; hyperbolic and degenerate caustics are excluded.

This research note proves the primitive interpretation of the experimentally recorded invariant k114 in Reznik–Garcia–Koiller (2020/2021), establishes the exact period classification, and gives an exact doubled-triangle counterexample to the unrestricted six-event return interpretation. It applies Stachel's published parametrization, classical Jacobi identities and established meromorphic divisor methods. No new-method or exclusive historical priority claim is made. The bounded primary-source audit found no explicit earlier proof of this exact target; novelty of the specific formulation is not certified. Full text of one related 2023 Dragović–Gajić article was unavailable, and the accompanying priority note records that coverage gap.

The deposit contains the manuscript PDF and a support archive with standalone LaTeX source, exact finite arithmetic controls, independent supplementary theta-series diagnostics, recorded outputs, metadata, references and priority-search limits. Finite checks support the analytic all-period proof; floating-point computations are not validated numerical certification.

whole_original_scholarly_typed_object.name: An exact period criterion for focal-distance products in elliptic billiards
whole_original_scholarly_typed_object.headline: An exact period criterion for focal-distance products in elliptic billiards
whole_original_scholarly_typed_object.description: An exact least-period criterion classifies when ordinary focal-distance products are constant in noncircular elliptic billiards, including primitive windings and repetitions.
whole_original_scholarly_typed_object.abstract: For a noncircular elliptic billiard with a strictly nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic, we prove that the product of ordinary distances from all vertices to either fixed focus is independent of phase if and only if the least period is 2 modulo 4. This proves the least-period interpretation of entry k₁₁₄ in Reznik–Garcia–Koiller's list of unproved invariants and classifies every other primitive period and every repeated traversal. The proof identifies the complete divisor of the focal-distance factor in the classical Jacobi parameter. An exact doubled-triangle example shows why a condition on return length alone is insufficient. The parametrization, identities and divisor method are established tools. This AI-assisted research note is unrefereed.

whole_original_public_sections.heading: What the result says
paragraphs: A billiard trajectory inside an ellipse bounces according to the usual reflection law. In a confocal family, every side touches the same inner ellipse, called the caustic. Moving the starting point changes the polygon’s phase while retaining that caustic.

This note asks when the product of the distances from all polygon vertices to one fixed focus stays unchanged as the phase moves. The answer depends on the least period: the number of bounces before the trajectory first returns. Counting a repeated traversal as a longer list can give the wrong answer.

whole_original_public_sections.heading: The full theorem
paragraphs: Fix outer and inner ellipses x²/a²+y²/b²=1 and x²/A²+y²/B²=1, with a>b>0, A>B>0, a>A, b>B and a²−b²=A²−B²=c²>0. The caustic is strictly nested, nondegenerate and confocal. The foci F±=(±c,0) are fixed, and the factors are ordinary positive Euclidean distances from the original billiard vertices, not squared distances or distances from an outer tangent polygon.

For any actual periodic elastic billiard family tangent to that caustic, let n be its primitive least period and set Dₙ±(u)=∏ⱼ₌₀ⁿ⁻¹ |Pⱼ(u)−F±|. Each focal product is independent of phase if and only if n≡2 (mod 4). Every admissible primitive coprime star winding and both orientations are included; n=1 and n=2 cannot occur in this strict elliptical-caustic setting.

For every even least period, Dₙ⁺(u)=Dₙ⁻(u) at each phase. This includes n≡0 (mod 4), when the equal products still vary with phase. Equality between the two foci is a different assertion from phase constancy.

For every integer r≥1, an r-fold traversal gives (Dₙ±)ʳ. Positivity makes this power operation injective, so repetition preserves the primitive constancy class in both directions. For a listed return length N≡2 (mod 4), constancy holds exactly when its least period is even.

whole_original_public_sections.heading: Why least period controls the product
paragraphs: The proof uses Stachel’s classical Jacobi parametrization P(u)=(−a sn u,b cn u), with modulus k=c/A∈(0,1), K=K(k), K′=K(√(1−k²)), cn(v)=B/b and 0<v<K. Here a=A dn(v)/cn(v), and successive vertices are separated by δ=2v=4Kτ/n, where gcd(τ,n)=1 and 0<τ<n/2. Reversing orientation gives the same cyclic subgroup.

The manuscript checks that the tangent contacts lie inside the actual chords and that the two inward rays satisfy elastic reflection across the normal. Real injectivity modulo 4K makes n the true vertex period. The geometric calculation gives the positive ordinary-distance factors g±(u)=a±c sn u; a>c prevents a hidden sign or square-root convention.

On the sn torus ℂ/(4Kℤ+2iK′ℤ), the factor g₊ has two simple poles p=iK′ and p+2K, and two distinct simple zeros p−K±v. These are complete, because zero and pole degrees agree. This torus is used for the focal factor; the full complex boundary map need not have the same imaginary period.

Writing H=⟨δ⟩ for the n-element orbit subgroup, translating the complete divisor through H gives one double zero coset, represented by z=−1/4+τ/(2n), and pole cosets H and 1/2+H. For odd n there are 2n uncancelled simple poles. For even n there are n double poles, cancelled exactly when (−n+2τ)/4 is an integer: precisely n≡2 (mod 4).

A divisor-free meromorphic function on the compact connected torus is constant. In the other classes a pole remains; the identity theorem transfers that nonconstancy to the physical real family. The half-period identity g₋(u)=g₊(u+2K) gives the second focus and the even-period pointwise equality. This is an all-period proof, rather than an extrapolation from finite checks.
For n=2m≡2 (mod 4), the positive constant can be evaluated as ∏ⱼ₌₀ᵐ⁻¹ [a²−c² sn²(2jv)]. It has units of lengthⁿ.

whole_original_public_sections.heading: Why a listed return length of six is insufficient
paragraphs: Take a=√15, b=√7, c=√8, A²=135/16 and B²=7/16. The triangle with vertices (a,0), (−3a/4,7/4), (−3a/4,−7/4), and its central reflection, are primitive three-bounce trajectories in the same fixed confocal family. Their side lines x=−A and x±ay=a are tangent to the caustic, their contact points lie inside the segments, and the inward unit rays satisfy the physical reflection law.

At the fixed focus F₊ their positive primitive products are 15a/2+3c and 15a/2−3c. Traversing each triangle twice produces six listed events, but the two products differ by (15a/2+3c)²−(15a/2−3c)²=90ac=180√30>0.

Thus a return length of six alone does not force phase constancy. The example distinguishes an unrestricted repeated-list interpretation from a statement explicitly about primitive least period; it does not refute that primitive statement.

whole_original_public_sections.heading: Circle and other boundaries
paragraphs: For a circle the two foci coincide with its center, every focal distance is the radius a, and every listed N-event product is aᴺ. This is a separate elementary case: the noncircular pole argument is not continued through c=0.

Hyperbolic or degenerate caustics, grazing or two-bounce limits and uniform lower bounds on the size of phase variation are outside the theorem. Ordinary floating-point agreement does not certify constancy, especially when real variation is below numerical resolution. No validated numerical bounds or proof-assistant formalization are claimed.

whole_original_public_sections.heading: Context and credit
paragraphs: Reznik, Garcia and Koiller recorded the focal product as k₁₁₄. Their final 2021 Arnold Mathematical Journal article, Fifty New Invariants of N-Periodics in the Elliptic Billiard, defines ordinary vertex-to-focus distances and lists the 2-mod-4 observation in Table 2 with an unknown proof entry. Its text does not explicitly resolve primitive least period versus a return list allowing repetitions. The earlier v11 preprint has the different title Eighty New Invariants; editions are not silently substituted.

Stachel’s published 2022 Theorem 4.3 and equation (4.9) supply the classical parametrization. Standard Jacobi periods, shifts and addition identities, and the general meromorphic Poncelet pole-removal method, retain prior credit. Schwartz, Akopyan–Schwartz–Tabachnikov and Roitman–Garcia–Reznik provide method precedents. The target-specific calculation is the focal divisor and its orbit-coset arithmetic; no new elliptic-function method is claimed.

Other products have different factors: k₁₁₅ concerns vertices of the outer tangent polygon, k₁₁₇ concerns caustic-contact lengths, and k₂₀₂ concerns perpendicular distances to sides. Ferudun’s related unrefereed note addresses k₁₁₅, rather than the original billiard-vertex product here.

The source comparison is bounded. No exclusive historical priority, influence, exhaustive literature coverage or present worldwide openness is certified. The full billiard body of the related Dragović–Gajić article remained unavailable, and the inspected author-site Ferudun body was not authenticated as the exact Zenodo-deposit bytes. These limits do not become claims that the unread material is irrelevant.

records.full_native_deposit_description_HTML:
For a noncircular elliptic billiard with a strictly nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic, the product of ordinary distances from all vertices to either fixed focus is independent of phase if and only if the primitive least period is congruent to 2 modulo 4. The result covers all admissible primitive star turns and both orientations. For every even least period, the two focal products are equal at each phase. Repetitions raise the positive primitive product to an integer power, so listed return length alone is insufficient. Circles are treated separately; hyperbolic and degenerate caustics are excluded.

This research note proves the primitive interpretation of the experimentally recorded invariant k114 in Reznik–Garcia–Koiller (2020/2021), establishes the exact period classification, and gives an exact doubled-triangle counterexample to the unrestricted six-event return interpretation. It applies Stachel's published parametrization, classical Jacobi identities and established meromorphic divisor methods. No new-method or exclusive historical priority claim is made. The bounded primary-source audit found no explicit earlier proof of this exact target; novelty of the specific formulation is not certified. Full text of one related 2023 Dragović–Gajić article was unavailable, and the accompanying priority note records that coverage gap.

The deposit contains the manuscript PDF and a support archive with standalone LaTeX source, exact finite arithmetic controls, independent supplementary theta-series diagnostics, recorded outputs, metadata, references and priority-search limits. Finite checks support the analytic all-period proof; floating-point computations are not validated numerical certification.

AI tools were used extensively in solving, drafting, source comparison, reproduction and independent adversarial reviews. This preprint is unrefereed and has not undergone conventional human peer review. The author is responsible for its claims.
